title: Signal cartography for launch thresholds and KPI butterflies
content:
One-line summary: lightweight, visual mapping (cartography) of launch signals with threshold heuristics and small 'butterfly' contingency actions to reduce noise and speed decisions.

Context / Why this exists
- We keep getting late-stage alarms that are noisy (alerts that trigger for transient token-cost spikes or short-lived latency blips) and the on-call/product ops handoff is slow.
- This doc experiments with a compact, prioritized signal map that ties metric thresholds to a short list of deterministic actions (the butterflies) by launch phase. Works as both a KPI tracker and a checklist for go/no-go decisions.

Audience
- Product ops, release engineers, on-call SREs, solutions eng for customer betas, and the launch PM.

Scope
- Focused on feature launches that touch hosted API + dedicated routing (so metrics include cost per 1k tokens, model-fallback rate, and route error uplift). Not a full enterprise go-live audit.

How to use this doc (quickstart)
1) Before canary: populate baseline numbers from the last 30d for the feature route(s). Capture medians and 95th percentiles.
2) Stage1 (beta): apply soft thresholds (yellow) and subscribe only product-ops and feature owners.
3) Stage2 (wide-canary): apply stronger thresholds (orange) and notify SRE + Solutions Eng progressively.
4) Go-live: hard thresholds (red) and execute butterflies if triggered.

KPI catalog + example thresholds (single-line explanation + rationale):
- End-to-end p95 latency (ms): yellow 150ms over baseline, orange 300ms, red 600ms. Rationale: user-facing latency impacts conversion; p95 chosen to catch tail.
- Route error rate (% of 500/5xx): yellow 0.5% absolute increase, orange 1.5%, red 3%. Rationale: brief 0.5% spike tolerable during canaries.
- Model-fallback ratio (requests that used fallback model): yellow 2%, orange 5%, red 10%. Rationale: fallback preserves SLA but indicates quality/capacity mismatch.
- Token cost / 1k tokens (USD): yellow +12% over projected, orange +25%, red +50%. Rationale: cost overruns degrade unit economics and may require throttling.
- Throughput saturation (% of pool capacity): yellow 65%, orange 80%, red 95%. Rationale: keep headroom for spikes and autoscale delays.
- Quality regression (eval set delta, relative): yellow 1.5% drop, orange 3% drop, red 5% drop. Rationale: small regressions acceptable in early beta, but not at GA.
- User adoption (DAU for feature): green if trending upwards, yellow if flat, red if decline >10% week-over-week.

Buttery actions (short deterministic steps mapped to thresholds)
- Yellow (informational): ping feature owner and product-ops slack channel, start 15-min watch, capture logs and a small sample of requests to S3. No customer-facing action.
- Orange (active mitigation): enable reduced concurrency on the feature route (soft throttle to 60%), switch to cheaper quantized variant for non-critical requests, open a short incident in PagerDuty with SE/infra watch.
- Red (protect & rollback): route traffic to stable rollout percentage (rollback to previous model or route fully to fallback), pause new enrollments, invoke cross-region fallback, and trigger billing-limit throttle if token cost runaway.

Signal cartography table (minimal, meant to be copied into a sheet)
- Column headers: signal | baseline metric | current | delta | threshold-level | butterfly | owner | action-ticket
- Example row: p95 latency | 220ms | 520ms | +300ms | red | route to fallback | Jonah Kim | JIRA-3890

Operational notes and gotchas
- Metric lag: most cost and billing signals are 10-30m delayed. Use proxy metrics (e.g., per-replica GPU utilization + prefix cache hit rate) for real-time heuristics.
- False positives: short-lived token-cost spikes often correlate with a single customer testing high-volume batch jobs. Use request sampling to identify origin and consider temporary customer throttles before global throttling.
- Quality vs cost tradeoffs: Butterflies that switch to quantized models reduce cost but often decrease quality; include immediate A/B evaluation slices during orange to track impact.

Runbook snippets (short checklist for on-call or product ops)
- Step 0: confirm alert validity (check sample requests + correlated infra metrics).
- Step 1: classify signal severity using this doc's thresholds.
- Step 2: pick butterfly and assign owner (owner must ack in 5m for orange/red).
- Step 3: execute mitigation, record start time, and update the incident ticket with expected rollback conditions.
- Step 4: after mitigation, run quality eval subset (10 prompts) to validate no severe quality regression.
- Step 5: if mitigated for >30m, schedule a postmortem and capacity forecast update.

Pre-launch checklist (short curated items)
- Baseline capture completed for 30d (owner: product-ops)
- Traffic shaping plan and autoscale headroom validated with infra (owner: infra)
- Cost guardrails configured in billing console (owner: finance-ops)
- Canary cohort defined and % ramp plan documented (owner: PM)
- Quick-eval prompt set created and added to the quality monitoring job (owner: research-ml)
- Communication plan for customers prepared (owner: solutions-eng)

Decision heuristics (simple if/then rules)
- If cost > orange AND traffic is concentrated to <3 customers -> contact those customers before global throttle.
- If p95 latency exceeds red for >2 consecutive 5m windows -> execute rollback butterfly.
- If fallback ratio increases >10% instantaneously but end-to-end errors are stable -> investigate model routing mismatch before throttling.

Open questions (to resolve before GA)
- Do we want hard automatic throttles on cost red, or require manual product ops approval? Current default: manual for new launches, auto for established GA routes.
- Should we compute thresholds as absolute deltas or percentile-relative deltas per customer segment? (pro: segment deltas reduce noisy cross-customer signals)
- How to store the per-feature quick-eval sets so they are accessible to on-call without heavy UI friction?

Next steps (action items)
- [Asha] create a canonical sheet with the signal cartography table and wire the p95/p99 and token-cost feeds (JIRA-3912).
- [Jonah] run 2 trial canaries next week and simulate orange/red butterflies in staging to measure rollback times (JIRA-3913).
- [Sofia] document customer notification templates for the three severity tiers and attach to the playbook (Confluence draft).

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep the butterflies small — they should be high-confidence, reversible, and low blast radius.
- Avoid sprawl: start with 6 signals then expand only if we consistently use them during canaries.

References and useful links
- billing runbook (internal) — see linked_confluence above
- prior incident postmortem: JIRA-2781 (model-fallback storm)

End of doc.

Revision history
